lead: Providence plumbing deals with old triple-deckers, lead service lines and cold New England winters. PipeMend sends licensed local plumbers across Providence.
risk: lead service lines, frozen pipes and aging pipes in multi-family homes
risk_short: lead lines, frozen pipes and old pipes
why: The East Side, Federal Hill and Elmhurst have homes and triple-deckers from the 1850s to the 1930s with galvanized supply lines, cast-iron stacks and lead service lines in many cases.
Winter cold freezes pipes near exterior walls and on porches. Coastal storms flood low areas near the rivers and the bay.
water: Providence Water treats water from the Scituate Reservoir. It is very soft. The utility has a large lead service line replacement program.
tips: Check Providence Water's lead line lookup.
Keep the heat on in every unit through winter.
Know where each unit's shutoff is.
areas: PipeMend works on the East Side and in Fox Point, Federal Hill, Elmhurst, Mount Pleasant, Washington Park, Olneyville and every other neighborhood.
permits: Plumbing permits come from the City of Providence Department of Inspection and Standards, and plumbers are licensed by the Rhode Island Department of Labor and Training.

faq.q: Is Providence replacing lead water lines?
faq.a: Yes. Providence Water has a program to replace lead service lines across its system, and you can look up your address. A plumber can also check where the line enters your basement.
